evals.description: Supergut case study, Founder/CEO persona. Brief surfaces creative engine bottleneck as top pain.

input.case_study_outcome: Paused $100k/mo meta spend → $1m/mo NCR in 3 months
input.literal_mechanism: Used 1,000 unpaid micro-influencer videos as paid creative on meta, combined with Cost Cap campaigns per SKU to keep CAC controlled while scaling spend
brief_top_pains: Creative engine is the bottleneck — can't produce enough variants to scale spend
CAC creeps up the moment we push more budget
Burned by previous agencies who couldn't sustain results past month 3
Don't know what's actually scalable vs. one-hit-wonder

expected_output.notes: Top pain is creative engine bottleneck — Pattern 1 (Contrarian Refresh: 'instead of agency-produced creative') is the highest-leverage. Pattern 3 (Constraint Negation: 'without an in-house creative team') is close second. Pattern 5 (Position Engineering: 'turned customers into the creative engine') is a strong third.

evals.description: Sweet Bee Organics case study, Founder/CEO persona. Mechanism involves ramping spend while cutting CAC.

input.case_study_outcome: $2m to $21m/yr in 1 year. Net new customer revenue $300k → $1.5m. Ad spend $25k → $500k in 3 months while cutting CAC by ~75%
input.literal_mechanism: Restructured meta campaigns from broad audiences to tightly-segmented ones around buyer intent, then layered creative testing at high volume to find scalable winners before pouring spend behind them
brief_top_pains: CAC creeps up the moment we push more budget
Don't know which creatives are scalable vs. one-hit-wonder
Burned by agencies who couldn't sustain results
Can't justify spending more until we trust the system

expected_output.notes: Top pain is CAC at scale — Pattern 3 (Constraint Negation: '20x spend without CAC moving') is highest-leverage. Pattern 2 (Hidden Misattribution: 'testing creative before spending, not after') strong. Pattern 7 (Named Methodology) works for the strategist who wants a soft teaser.

evals.description: Grüns case study, Marketing Leader persona. Mechanism is launch / 0-to-1 scale.

input.case_study_outcome: $0 → $2m revenue in first 2 months from launch
input.literal_mechanism: Built launch creative engine from day one — ran 50+ ad variants in the first 2 weeks, tested across multiple hooks and angles, found the winning creative direction before any major spend, then scaled the winners with cost-controlled campaigns
brief_top_pains: Need to launch new products / brands and don't know if creative will hit
Last launch underperformed because we picked the wrong creative direction early
Can't afford to burn the launch budget testing in production
Need to find winning creative fast — before momentum dies

expected_output.notes: Top pain is wrong creative direction picked early — Pattern 2 (Hidden Misattribution: 'finding the winner before scaling, not after') is highest-leverage. Pattern 3 (Constraint Negation: 'without burning the launch budget') strong. Pattern 8 (Plain English: 'tested 50+ ad variants in the first 2 weeks') is the safety net.

evals.description: Stress test: literal mechanism is too vague to wordsmith. Skill should kick back, not invent.

input.literal_mechanism: Worked closely with the brand on their marketing

expected_output.expected_behavior: Skill stops at Step 0. Returns: 'Literal mechanism is too vague to wordsmith. Need: what specifically did the agency do? Channel, tactic, named approach, or specific number. Send the strategist back to Layer A / case study extraction.'
expected_output.notes: This eval verifies the skill does not invent mechanisms when the input is empty. Garbage in must produce a kick-back, not a hallucination out.

v1_acceptance_criteria.pass_threshold: 3 of 4 evals produce a menu meeting their expected_output (the stress test counts as 'pass' if the skill correctly kicks back)
v1_acceptance_criteria.iteration_trigger: Below 3/4 pass rate, or strategist rejects all variants and writes their own — log the variant they wrote and which pattern it matches (or whether it's a new pattern to add to the library)
